children.title: Paramount Settles Trump’s 60 Minutes Lawsuit for $16 Million
children.description_medium: On July 2, 2025, Paramount agreed to pay $16 million to settle Donald Trump’s lawsuit over CBS’s editing of a 60 Minutes interview.  Reuters reported that Paramount said the payment would be allocated to Trump’s future presidential library and that the company would not apologize.
children.description_long: On July 2, 2025, Paramount agreed to pay $16 million to settle Donald Trump’s lawsuit over CBS’s editing of a 60 Minutes interview. Reuters reported that Paramount said the payment would be allocated to Trump’s future presidential library and that the company would not apologize. The settlement was a discrete legal and corporate action, separate from Congress’s later rescission of public-broadcasting funds and the White House’s media-bias tracker. The supplied Reuters report supports the settlement amount and the stated allocation. It does not support combining this payment with the separate ABC settlement into the original card’s $32 million headline. These records concern different actors and mechanisms: a private settlement of Trump’s lawsuit, a law rescinding previously approved spending, and a White House communications webpage. The supplied sources date each action and support the reported amounts or webpage description. They do not establish a single January 2025 event encompassing the year’s media-related developments. The card’s $32 million settlement headline also does not match the $16 million Paramount settlement reported here and the separate $15 million ABC library contribution described in the claims. Other actions named in the original card remain outside these drafts where event-specific sourcing is insufficient.

children.title: Trump Signs Rescission Cutting About $1.1 Billion in Public-Broadcasting Funding
children.description_medium: On July 24, 2025, President Donald Trump signed legislation canceling about $9 billion in previously approved spending, including roughly $1. 1 billion for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.  The Associated Press report published by PBS NewsHour described the signed rescission and the public-broadcasting amount.  This funding action is distinct from media-company settlements and later White House criticism of news outlets.
children.description_long: On July 24, 2025, President Donald Trump signed legislation canceling about $9 billion in previously approved spending, including roughly $1.1 billion for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting. children.title: White House Launches Media-Bias Tracker and “Offender” Page
children.description_medium: On November 28, 2025, the White House launched a webpage identifying outlets and reports it characterized as misleading or biased, including a section described as an “Offender Hall of Shame. ” The Washington Post reported the launch and Trump’s expanded criticism of reporters.  This is a discrete communications action, separate from the July Paramount settlement and the signed rescission affecting public broadcasting.
